statement: User objectives become explicit milestones and traceable, testable Tasks before autonomous execution. The user can correct priorities, goals and operating mode.
A Planner chooses technical direction and reviews completion; a Supervisor coordinates and reports; the Engine authorizes state changes; Workers execute bounded assignments.
A project in Zero-Cost Mode must never send any request through an unverified or potentially paid AI route.
In-house Planner conversations and exact OpenCode Worker sessions must be inspectable in RelayX with histories, attempts and evidence.
Work remains recoverable across pause, stop, process restart and provider disruption.
On any transport failure, Worker stall, or unusable Worker report, the next recovery decision belongs to the Planner.
User-defined boundaries and system invariants outrank any AI-generated instruction.
The Engine alone may claim tasks, commit transitions, authorize dispatch and enforce costs.
Failures cannot directly re-arm a Worker; a Planner decision is required before any corrective Worker assignment.
Hard zero-paid-inference limits include Planner, Supervisor, Workers, evaluators and fallbacks.
Every executable Task has acceptance criteria, dependency edges and a tracked priority.
One active execution slot per pair in V1; atomic claims prevent double-dispatch.
Tasks become DONE only after correlated verification plus Planner and any required human approval.
Planner/Worker messages move through the new server-native/API adapters; no Chrome/DOM/AppleScript clipboard messaging is required.
Keep legacy GUI transport independent and the disabled OpenCode CLI delivery method disabled, with neither acting as an implicit fallback.
Worker identity uses exact external session ID; title is display metadata and can change.
A structured Worker question resumes the same waiting question/run rather than generating a new assignment.
In Zero-Cost Mode, any unknown, stale, mixed, paid or promotional-credit-only route is non-dispatchable unless a separate explicit user-approved rule covers it.
Model catalogs and benchmark popularity are discovery evidence, not authority for account-specific cost.
Exhausted free quotas cause queue/pausing or a verified-free switch; no paid fallback.
Each qualification must be time-bound, explainable and rechecked on relevant errors.
Model ranking must distinguish Supervisor planning, Planner reasoning, coding, debugging, frontend implementation and tool/question reliability.
A success means verified and accepted artifacts, not a model statement claiming completion.
Show sample size, evidence recency and uncertainty; do not treat 2/2 as proven reliability.
Every actionable incident has exact affected attempt/assignment/session IDs, evidence packet, classification and Planner decision correlation.
The reconciler may observe and resolve exact evidence but cannot manufacture a receipt or blindly replay an ambiguous send.
Pause/Stop suppresses new dispatch; restart reconciliation precedes new work.
Mutations are idempotent, actor-attributed and auditable.
Every external event is correlated to exact session/provider identity and attempt.
Credentials never appear in model prompts, benchmark fixture snapshots, user-visible reports or stored tool transcripts.
On startup, outstanding Delivery/Attempt intents reconcile before new scheduling.
At all times display pair lifecycle state (`STOPPED`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` etc.), task state, attempted delivery state, current model route and blocking reason independently.
Show both Planner and Worker latest messages; allow composing a **new** custom intervention after pause/stop. Never mutate historical transcripts.
User can trace each Task → Assignment → Attempt → Delivery → Evidence → Planner decision.
Distinguish `catalog listed`, `verified free`, `qualified`, `available`, and `recommended` model states.
